title: Study government's role in keeping markets concentrated
proposal: The chapter says the FTC must consider how government itself, including regulation and compliance costs, helps keep markets concentrated in fields such as pharmaceuticals, health care, banking, and real estate brokerage.
quote: The FTC must consider, therefore, the role of government itself in maintaining market concentration

title: Expand the consumer welfare standard beyond price
proposal: The chapter says the consumer welfare standard should still guide the FTC, but in some cases with strong evidence it should consider more than just prices. It also says companies' claimed efficiencies should meet the same standard of proof as claimed harms.
quote: in appropriate situations and with strong evidence, this standard must be expanded to include more factors than just price.

title: Option: move all antitrust enforcement to the Justice Department
proposal: The chapter reports that some conservatives want antitrust enforcement handled only by the Justice Department, ending the FTC's role or its independent status. The chapter itself argues conservatives should still use the FTC's power for now.
quote: Some conservatives think that antitrust enforcement should be invested solely in the Department of Justice (DOJ).
contested: View of some conservatives; the chapter argues against giving up FTC power for now

title: Create an FTC task force on ESG/DEI collusion
proposal: The chapter says the FTC should set up a task force to investigate whether firms, especially in private equity, use environmental, social, and governance (ESG) or diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI) practices to fix prices, reduce output, or meet targets together.
quote: The FTC should set up an ESG/DEI collusion task force to investigate firms—particularly in private equity

title: Have Congress investigate ESG as cover for anticompetitive conduct
proposal: The chapter says Congress should investigate whether ESG practices are being used to hide anticompetitive behavior or unfair trade practices.
quote: Congress should investigate ESG practices as a cover for anticompetitive activity and possible unfair trade practices.

title: Treat some politically based refusals of service as unfair practices
proposal: The chapter says that when banks or internet platforms refuse customers over political or social views, it can be an unfair trade practice if the business is publicly traded, highly regulated, legally privileged, has market power, and acts on an unrelated political agenda.
quote: This type of behavior can rise to the level of an unfair trade practice when the business is (1) publicly traded; (2) highly regulated;

title: Examine platforms' ads and contracts with children; require parent OK
proposal: The chapter says the FTC should examine whether online platforms' advertising and contracts with children are deceptive or unfair, possibly requiring written parental consent.
quote: The FTC should examine platforms' advertising and contract-making with children as a deceptive or unfair trade practice, perhaps requiring written parental consent.
contested: Chapter notes some conservatives are skeptical of regulating children's online use and prefer an FTC education role

title: Bring cases against firms contracting with kids without parent consent
proposal: The chapter says the FTC should start unfair trade practice proceedings against companies that enter into contracts with children without parental consent.
quote: The FTC can and should institute unfair trade practices proceedings against entities that enter into contracts with children without parental consent.
contested: Chapter notes some conservatives are skeptical of regulating children's online use and prefer an FTC education role

title: Option: FTC education programs for parents online
proposal: The chapter reports that limited-government conservatives would rather the FTC play an educational role, such as sharing best practices or programs to help parents online, instead of regulating.
quote: Limited-government conservatives would prefer the FTC play an educational role instead.
contested: Alternative view within the chapter; other contributors favor FTC action on children's online contracts

title: Create an FTC role for working with state attorneys general
proposal: The chapter says the FTC Chairman's office should have a dedicated role for cooperating with state attorneys general and should invite them to discuss enforcement in areas like Big Tech and hospital and supermarket mergers.
quote: this would mean establishing a distinct role in the FTC Chairman's office focused on state AG cooperation

title: Return authority to FTC regional offices
proposal: The chapter says the FTC should consider giving more authority back to its regional offices, which it says are more in touch with local issues.
quote: The FTC should consider returning authority to these offices.
contested: Chapter notes some contributors oppose expanding FTC regional offices

title: Improve how the FTC measures consumer benefit from platforms
proposal: The chapter says the FTC must get better at measuring consumer benefit and be open to behavioral explanations, such as habit, for how online platforms gain and keep market power.
quote: The FTC must become more sophisticated in measuring consumer surplus.
